title: Is one in five a lot or a little?
hook: One friendship in five crosses groups. Is that low, or about what chance gives?

doesNotKnow: that the yardstick for 'friends sort by group' is the cross-group share random pairing would give (about 2pq)

misconception: If one in five friendships crosses groups, that is about what you'd expect when one in three people is in the smaller group.
objective: The learner can explain that with 20 and 10 students, random friendships would cross groups about 46% of the time (200 of 435 pairs), so a class where 9 of 45 friendships cross (20%) shows homophily: the gap from the chance yardstick is the evidence.

claims.text: With 20 and 10 students there are 435 possible pairs, and 10 × 20 = 200 of them (46%) cross groups: each of the 10 can pair with each of the 20. On stage 'Count possible pairs' draws those 200 pairs.
claims.source: C(30,2) = 435; 20 x 10 = 200 cross pairs; 200/435 = 0.4598. Builder's node check, 2026-10-14. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): node: C(30,2) = 435, 20 x 10 = 200, 200/435 = 0.4598 -> 46%. | v2: Demo.tsx CROSS_PAIRS.length = 200, PAIRS.length = 435; the pairs view draws CROSS_PAIRS. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: 435 pairs, 200 cross (45.98%). The pairs view draws CROSS_PAIRS; the reveal's '10 x 20 = 200 lines you counted' is backed by the required 'pairs' milestone.

claims.text: The stage's real class has 45 friendships, 9 of them crossing groups (20%).
claims.source: Lesson rule (brief): a made-up class. Demo.tsx REAL lays out 28 friendships inside the 20, 8 inside the 10 and 9 crossing, placed with mulberry32(7). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Re-ran Demo.tsx REAL with mulberry32(7): 45 distinct friendships, 9 crossing (28 in A, 8 in B). 9/45 = 20%. Made-up class is a convention.

claims.text: In a random class each of the 45 friendships is an independent random pair, so on average about 46% cross groups. The reveal quotes the learner's largest recorded run (on the QA path 1,001 classes, average 46%, none with 9 or fewer, fewest 11), kept after Start over.
claims.source: Lesson rule (Demo.tsx drawClasses: each friendship a uniform pair of the 435, independently); the crossing count is Binomial(45, 200/435), mean 20.69. Builder's seeded run (mulberry32(41), first random class then 1,000 more, the QA path): 1,001 classes averaging 20.88 crossing (46%). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): drawClasses draws each of 45 friendships uniformly from 435 pairs, independently (repeats possible). Mean 45 x 200/435 = 20.69. Own seeded run mulberry32(41): first class 26, 1,001 classes average 20.877 (46.4%). | v2: v2: the record is set when classes are drawn and Start over does not clear it. Builder node re-run of mulberry32(41), 2026-10-14: 1,001 classes average 46%, fewest 11, 0 with 9 or fewer. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own run with mulberry32(41): the first class has 26 crossing; 1,001 classes average 46.39%, 0 with 9 or fewer, fewest 11. rec is replaced only by a larger run and Start over reseeds 41, so the same 1,001 classes give the same record. Binomial mean 45 x 200/435 = 20.69 (46%).

claims.text: If each of 45 friendships crosses groups with chance 46%, 9 or fewer crossing has probability about 1 in 4,000.
claims.source: Exact binomial, builder's node run 2026-10-14: P(X <= 9) for X ~ Binomial(45, 200/435) = 0.000264 (1 in 3,790). Matches the strand manager's edit in company/domains/briefs/probability.statistics.md (0.00026). Seeded run (seed 41, not chosen for its result): none of the first 1,001 random classes had 9 or fewer; the fewest was 11. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Exact binomial in node: P(X <= 9), X ~ Bin(45, 200/435) = 0.000264 (1 in 3,790) -> 'about 1 in 4,000' fair. Seed-41 run: 0 of 1,001 had <= 9, fewest 11.

claims.text: For large groups with shares 2/3 and 1/3 the chance share of crossing friendships is 2 x 2/3 x 1/3, about 44%.
claims.source: 2pq with p = 2/3, q = 1/3 gives 4/9 = 0.444 (derivation); the 2pq yardstick is from E&K ch. 4 (section unconfirmed). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): 2 x 2/3 x 1/3 = 4/9 = 0.444. E&K (2010) not opened (host blocked); from my own knowledge the 2pq homophily test is in ch. 4 ('Networks in Their Surrounding Contexts'), section 4.1 'Homophily'. Placement: confident.

claims.text: A cross-group share well below the chance share is the evidence that friends sort by group (homophily).
claims.source: E&K ch. 4 homophily test (compare the observed cross-group fraction with 2pq). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): E&K ch. 4, section 4.1 (not opened; own knowledge): 'if the fraction of cross-gender edges is significantly less than 2pq, then there is evidence for homophily'. Learner sentence matches that test.

recall.question: A club is half red members and half blue. 15% of its friendships are red–blue. Is that evidence that friends stick to their own colour?
options: No: 15% is a normal share for two groups
Yes: random pairing would make about 50% cross
Only if red members have more friends
recall.why: The yardstick is the share of pairs that cross: 2pq = 2 x 1/2 x 1/2 = 50%. 15% is far below it, and that gap is the evidence.
